---
redu_schema: 2
repo: https://github.com/SamR1/FitTrackee
plan:
  tool: deploy_compose
  image: fittrackee/fittrackee:v1.3.4
  port: 5000
  vm: m1.medium
  flavor_id: "3"
  database: managed postgres WITH THE POSTGIS EXTENSION (redu-managed, own private VM, m1.small via db_flavor_id "2", db_extensions ["postgis"])
  hourly_cost_gbp: 0.0452
bootstrap:
  mcp: claude mcp add --transport http redu «REDACTED:env:78213b90» --client-id redu-mcp
  mcp_codex: codex mcp add redu --url «REDACTED:env:78213b90» --oauth-client-id redu-mcp
  source: fittrackee
quirks:
  - "⛔⛔ POSTGIS IS MANDATORY, AND A PLAIN MANAGED POSTGRES WILL NOT DO. Pass db_extensions ['postgis'] to deploy_compose. Migration 59 (fittrackee/migrations/versions/59_fed271354410_add_geometry_and_points_to_segments.py) adds a geoalchemy2 Geometry column and a geospatial GiST index, and FitTrackee NEVER runs CREATE EXTENSION itself: the only one in the repository is db/install_postgis_for_ci_e2e_package_tests.py, a CI helper. The entrypoint runs 'ftcli db upgrade || exit 1' before gunicorn (docker-entrypoint.sh:6), so without the extension the container exits 1 and crash-loops. That is the good news, because it fails loudly instead of coming up half-migrated. redu supports this: backend/src/services/cloud/pgExtensions.ts allows postgis and installs postgresql-<version>-postgis-3 plus CREATE EXTENSION at provision time, before your app ever connects."
  - "⛔ DATABASE_URL IS THE VARIABLE THAT SELECTS THE REAL DATABASE, and there is no SQLite fallback to worry about: fittrackee/config.py:127 sets SQLALCHEMY_DATABASE_URI from DATABASE_URL and nothing else, so an unset value fails at startup. The trap in THIS app is the other shape and it is just as expensive: upstream's compose ships its own postgis/postgis container (service fittrackee-db) whose data goes to a bind mount at ${HOST_DATABASE_DIR:-./data/db}, INSIDE the project directory, which is exactly what a source re-upload replaces and what dies with the VM. DELETE the fittrackee-db service, its depends_on entry and its volume. redu emits DATABASE_URL=postgresql://... (not postgres://, which SQLAlchemy 1.4+ rejects), so it can be passed straight through with no remapping. deploy_compose only APPENDS to the project .env and never edits your compose, so put DATABASE_URL: \"${DATABASE_URL}\" in the service's environment: block. An environment: entry beats env_file, which matters because upstream's .env.docker.example sets its own DATABASE_URL pointing at the container you just deleted."
  - "PROVE THE DATABASE WIRING AFTER BOOT, BOTH HALVES, BECAUSE AN ABSENCE ALONE IS NOT EVIDENCE. Positive half, which is also what proves your exec works at all: run the sqlalchemy one-liner in the redu.md body below. It prints the database name, the SERVER's own IP address via inet_server_addr(), and the user count. The address must be the private IP of the managed database VM, never a loopback or a docker bridge address. Negative half: 'sudo docker ps --format {{.Names}} | grep -c fittrackee-db' must be 0 AND 'sudo docker ps --format {{.Names}} | grep -c fittrackee' must be at least 1. If the second one is also 0 your command did not run and the first zero means nothing."
  - "⛔⛔ NOBODY BECOMES ADMINISTRATOR BY SIGNING UP. YOU CREATE THE OWNER AT DEPLOY TIME, WITH THE CLI. This is the opposite of Memos and Dify and it is worth reading twice. POST /api/auth/register (fittrackee/users/auth.py:106-220) creates an account with the DEFAULT role, which is plain 'user', and fittrackee/users/models.py:314 defaults is_active to False. With EMAIL_URL empty, which is this recipe's default, no confirmation email is ever sent, so an anonymous signup produces an account that CANNOT log in. The owner is created by you, after the container is healthy: 'sudo docker exec fittrackee ftcli users create <username> --email <email> --role owner'. docsrc/source/cli.rst says that account is already active and that the CLI works even when registration is disabled. Do this as part of the deploy, before you hand over the URL, and CONFIRM THE EMAIL WITH THE USER FIRST."
  - "⛔⛔ THE REGISTRATION SETTING HAS A FIRST-USER CARVE-OUT IN EFFECT, AND IT IS NOT AN ENV VAR. The setting is max_users on the app_config row. fittrackee/application/models.py:52-56 computes is_registration_enabled as (max_users == 0 OR nb_users < max_users), and the default is 0, meaning UNLIMITED, meaning open to the internet the moment the hostname resolves. TESTED AGAINST THE FIRST ACCOUNT: with max_users set to 1 and zero users, 0 < 1 is true, so registration is STILL OPEN. Setting max_users does not close the first slot, it only caps how many slots exist. THE ONLY THING THAT CLOSES THE FIRST SLOT IS FILLING IT. So the order is: create the owner with ftcli (which bypasses the limit entirely), THEN set max_users to the number of accounts the user actually wants. There is no env var and no provisioning file for this in v1.3.4; max_users is set through PATCH /api/config as an admin, which is what the script in the body does."
  - "TEST THE BEHAVIOUR, NOT THE FLAG. GET /api/config is anonymous and reports is_registration_enabled, which is a derived value and therefore exactly the kind of thing that reads correct while the behaviour is wrong. The check that means something is a real anonymous POST /api/auth/register, which must answer 403 with 'error, registration is disabled' (fittrackee/users/auth.py:167). The script in the body does it that way, requires HTTP 200 and a FitTrackee-shaped body first, treats 502 as 'still starting, re-run' and exits a distinct inconclusive code rather than passing when it cannot tell."
  - "SET APP_SECRET_KEY EXPLICITLY AND REUSE THE SAME VALUE ON EVERY REDEPLOY. .env.docker.example:15 ships it as the literal string 'PLEASE CHANGE ME', and the docs describe it as the key used in JWT generation, with a warning logged when it is too short. Change it between deploys and every issued token stops validating: everyone is logged out, and outstanding email-confirmation and password-reset links become dead. Generate one long random value, store it with the user, and pass the identical one next time."
  - "⛔ THE UPLOADS VOLUME NEEDS A CHOWN, AND WITHOUT IT THE APP LOOKS HEALTHY AND EVERY UPLOAD FAILS. Dockerfile:40-53 adds uid 1000 'fittrackee', sets USER fittrackee, and does NOT create /usr/src/app/uploads, /usr/src/app/logs or /usr/src/app/.staticmap_cache. A named volume mounted where the image has no directory is created root-owned, so the app cannot write into it. Upstream solves this with a post_start hook that chowns as root, which needs Docker Compose 2.30.0+ (their own header says so) and is not worth betting on. Instead add a tiny init service to the compose: image busybox:1.37, user: root, command 'chown -R 1000:1000 /uploads /cache', the same two named volumes mounted, and the app depending on it with condition: service_completed_successfully. Then set GUNICORN_LOG=- and leave APP_LOG unset, which the docs say removes the need for /usr/src/app/logs entirely, so you are down to two volumes."
  - "MIND WHERE UPLOAD_FOLDER ACTUALLY PUTS FILES. fittrackee/config.py:35-36 joins the literal 'uploads' onto whatever you give it, so UPLOAD_FOLDER=/usr/src/app/uploads means the files land in /usr/src/app/uploads/uploads. That is upstream's own arrangement and it is fine; just do not be surprised by it, and do not mount the volume one level too deep. STATICMAP_CACHE_DIR gets the second volume; it is a regenerable cache, so it is the one thing here you may lose without consequence."
  - "PORT 5000, AND PROBE /api/check-db RATHER THAN /api/ping. Both are anonymous. /api/ping answers 200 'pong!' without touching the database, so it goes green on an instance whose database wiring is broken. /api/check-db runs SELECT 1 and answers 500 'db unavailable' when it cannot (fittrackee/application/health_check.py). Upstream's own container healthcheck uses check-db. Note the alpine runtime image has BusyBox wget, so write container healthchecks with wget, not curl."
  - "SET UI_URL TO THE FULL PUBLIC HTTPS URL, WITH THE SCHEME. The docs are explicit that UI_URL must contain the url scheme. It is used for links in emails and for mentions in the interface. Generate the dname yourself in the full fittrackee-<8 lowercase alnum>.redu.cloud form so the value is known at deploy time; a bare label gets a random suffix appended by redu and will not match."
  - "⛔ IF YOU DELETE THE CUSTOM NETWORKS, DELETE BOTH. Upstream declares internal_network with 'internal: true', which has NO route off the VM, and puts the app on both networks so it can still reach the outside. The managed database is on redu's private network, i.e. off this VM, so an app service left on internal_network ALONE cannot reach its database at all, and the symptom is a connection timeout that reads as a network fault on a database that is up. With the bundled db service gone the split has nothing left to protect: drop both networks and let compose use its default."
  - "NO REDIS IN THIS RECIPE, AND HERE IS EXACTLY WHAT THAT COSTS. Upstream's compose comments say the minimal single-user setup is the app plus a database, and that redis and a second 'workers' service off the same image are what enable API rate limits, email sending, user data export and zipped workout-archive uploads. Everything else, including uploading individual workout files, works without them. ⚠️ Do NOT half-configure email: the docs warn that if EMAIL_URL is set and Redis is not available the application WILL NOT START, and that from 1.3.1 setting EMAIL_URL without SENDER_EMAIL also prevents startup. Leave EMAIL_URL empty. The documented upgrade is redis:'managed' plus a workers service running 'dramatiq fittrackee.tasks:broker', which adds another VM to the bill and therefore is the user's decision, not yours."
  - "UPLOAD LIMITS ARE SMALL BY DEFAULT AND THERE ARE TWO OF THEM. fittrackee/application/models.py:25-30 defaults max_single_file_size to 1048576 (1 MB) and max_zip_file_size to 10485760 (10 MB), both raisable in the admin interface. Upstream's own nginx example notes that a reverse proxy also caps the body size independently. redu's proxy is not configured by this recipe, so if a large archive upload fails with 413 while FitTrackee's own limits are high enough, that is the proxy in front and not the app."
  - "DISK COMES WITH THE FLAVOR AND IT IS WHERE THE PHOTOS GO. m1.medium is 40 GB. Workout files are small, but media attachments (added in 1.3.0) and the static-map cache live on the app VM's volume, not in Postgres, so a user planning to attach a lot of photos should hear that number BEFORE the deploy: growing it later is a volume resize, not a redeploy."
  - "NO migrate_command NEEDED. The entrypoint runs the alembic migrations itself on every start. Two consequences: the FIRST boot on a fresh database is slower than the container's own 5s/15s/3-retry healthcheck suggests, so give the deploy health check room; and the docs warn to back up before upgrading the image tag, because a version bump migrates in place."
  - "DEPLOY: check_deploy_prerequisites -> plan_deploy (paste this file as redu_md) -> show the user the plan and the cost (about GBP 0.045/hr, roughly GBP 33 a month; inside the no-card free trial) and WAIT for their yes -> deploy_compose with flavor_id '3' (m1.medium), database:'managed', db_engine:'postgres', db_flavor_id:'2' (m1.small; OMITTING db_flavor_id defaults the DB VM to the app flavor and doubles the bill), db_extensions ['postgis'], compose_engine 'docker', port 5000. ⚠️ plan_deploy will want to upsize a compose stack to m1.large once needs_compose is declared; passing flavor_id explicitly holds m1.medium, and m1.large would also put this ABOVE the trial ceiling for no benefit."
  - "SOURCE IS UPLOAD MODE, NOT GIT. Nothing is built from source; the official image is pulled. ## redu
redu.cloud — an EU-hosted, agent-native cloud. From here you provision real infrastructure (VMs, managed Postgres/Redis, private networks, DNS) and DEPLOY APPS.

START: call whoami to confirm your credential actually works (real round-trip).

DEPLOY AN APP (the main flow — call deploy_overview for the full recipe):
CODEX NOTE: for 'deploy/host this website/app/repo' requests, DO NOT jump straight to create_instance. Use check_deploy_prerequisites -> plan_deploy -> deploy_app/deploy_compose so the user sees the plan + cost first. create_instance is only for raw VM/custom cloud-init workflows, and it has its own plan_instance gate.
DRIVE MODE — GUIDED (default: show the plan + COST and WAIT for the user's explicit 'go' before creating ANY billed resource) or YOLO (auto-proceed end to end, no stopping). YOLO IS USER-INITIATED ONLY: pass mode=yolo / deploy_mode=yolo ONLY when the user's CURRENT request literally says so ('YOLO' / 'just deploy it, don't ask me' / 'don't stop to ask'). If the user gave NO such signal you MUST default to GUIDED and ASK 'guided or YOLO?' — you may NOT assume YOLO. 'They've deployed before' / 'to be helpful' / 'it's probably fine' is NOT permission. Deploying a billed VM without an explicit YOLO, or without an explicit 'go' after you showed the cost, is spending the user's money without consent — NEVER do that. Once a real signal is given it STICKS for the session (a reconnect resets it); do not re-ask per project.

Do NOT read or summarise them - redu parses them SERVER-SIDE and returns a short digest, a pin_dname that keeps a redeploy on the SAME public URL, and preflight fixes for known failure patterns in YOUR repo. Highest-value step in the flow; it costs one cat each. KEEP the redu.md bytes: pass them to get_deployment as redu_md at the end too, so redu merges the old file with the new deploy instead of you overwriting what previous deploys learned.
platform_facts: THE deploy VM RUNS DOCKER, NOT PODMAN. The compose project is named app-src, so containers are app-src-<service>-1 and volumes are app-src_<name>. Use `sudo docker ...` on the VM; podman is not installed. Several deploys rediscovered this independently.

SOURCE IS EITHER GIT OR UPLOAD, NEVER BOTH. For code that is not pushed, or is private, or needs fixing first: write the files locally, call prepare_upload, run the tar+curl block it returns, then pass the source_token and NO repo. ⚠️ prepare_upload EXCLUDES .env from the tarball by design, so secrets have to reach the VM another way (pass them to the deploy call, not in the tree).

A MANAGED DATABASE IS A SECOND VM WITH ITS OWN HOURLY RATE, and delete_deployment deliberately LEAVES IT BEHIND so your data survives the app. That means a teardown that stops at delete_deployment keeps billing a database nobody can reach. Call delete_database too, and say so to the user before either.

A MANAGED POSTGRES SERVES EXACTLY ONE DATABASE. pg_hba is evaluated before role privileges, so being superuser does not help. An app that wants a second database needs a second managed server. This has broken deploys that otherwise looked healthy.

get_deployment RETURNS THE MERGED redu.md ONLY WHEN IT FITS ITS RESPONSE BUDGET. Over budget - which is normal for a mature recipe or any large app - it withholds redu_md_markdown and returns redu_md_last_deploy_block plus redu_md_deploy_log_line instead. That is NOT an error and must not be retried: apply those two edits to the file on disk and change nothing else.

⛔ THE MERGE NEVER WRITES A NEW QUIRK. Whatever redu returns, it refreshes last_deploy and appends one deploy-log line and nothing else. Every gotcha YOUR run discovered has to be typed into the quirks list by hand before you commit, or it is lost - and that list is the only part of the file that makes the next deploy cheaper.
⛔ NEVER WRITE A CREDENTIAL INTO redu.md. It is committed and read by the next person and the next agent. Names of variables, yes; their values, never. Hand secrets to the user in the session instead.

plan_deploy OVER-SIZES A PULLED COMPOSE STACK. Measured 8 times out of 8: declaring needs_compose makes it quote m1.large, roughly double the real requirement, because it cannot see that the images are pulled rather than built. Show the user the plan, but size from the app's real memory figure when you have one.

THE MANAGED DATABASE PASSWORD IS ON THE VM, NOT IN THE API. list_databases returns private_ip, port, db_name and db_user and DELIBERATELY NOT the password, so an agent that looks for it there finds nothing and starts guessing. The deploy writes the whole connection set into the compose project's .env on the app VM. Call get_env_keys for the NAMES first (no SSH, values never leave the VM); only if you need an actual VALUE, SSH in (get_ssh_command) and read that one key, `sudo grep '^PGPASSWORD=' /opt/app-src/.env`. ⚠️ That file is chmod 600 root:root so it needs sudo, and the database is on the PRIVATE network - reachable from the app VM, never from a laptop.

YOU CAN READ A DEPLOY VM WITHOUT SSHING INTO IT, and four tools do it: get_containers (what is running, health, restarts, crashed ones included), get_container_logs (what the app actually printed - the tool for 'deployed fine but does not work'), get_resource_usage (memory, disk, load, OOM kills) and get_env_keys (which variables got wired, by name). ⛔ get_instance_logs is the SERIAL CONSOLE and is not your app's logs; build_log stops when the build does. SSH is still yours for everything else - a shell on a real machine is the point, not a fallback. ⭐ MEASURED over 38 deploys: of 241 ssh escapes, 146 (61%) were exactly these four things, and the four tools were called 11 times. They are faster than a login, they cost the VM nothing extra (the reading is already cached), and reaching for ssh to run `docker ps` is the single most common wasted minute in a deploy.

⛔ THE PRIMARY SURFACE'S HOSTNAME COMES FROM THE TOP-LEVEL dname, NOT FROM expose[0].dname, WHICH IS SILENTLY DISCARDED. Extra expose entries DO keep the dname you give them, so the two behave differently and nothing tells you. If an app bakes its own public URL into config at boot (CPAD_MAIN_DOMAIN, allowed_origins, SITE_URL), generate the full `<label>-<8 lowercase letters/digits>.redu.cloud` form yourself and pass it as the TOP-LEVEL dname, which is used verbatim. Passing it on expose[0] instead gets you an app configured for a hostname redu never created, answering 200 on a name it does not believe is its own.

WEBSOCKETS WORK THROUGH THE PROXY WITH NO CONFIGURATION: every proxy host redu creates has upgrade enabled. Measured at the protocol level, HTTP/1.1 101 Switching Protocols with the subprotocol echoed back. ⚠️ TEST IT WITH `curl --http1.1`: plain curl negotiates HTTP/2, which has no Upgrade mechanism at all, so the app answers as an ordinary GET and the failure looks exactly like a proxy refusing to upgrade. Browsers use HTTP/1.1 for websockets regardless. Do not disable an app's realtime features on the strength of an HTTP/2 curl.

=== compose ===
# docker compose for production
# (minimal version: Docker Compose version 2.30.0)
#
# minimal application (for single user) only needs fittrackee and fittrackee-db containers.
#
# for multi-users application, uncomment the following containers:
# - fittrackee-workers for user data export, archive uploads and email sending (EMAIL_URL must be set in .env to enable emails)
# - fittrackee-redis container for API rate limits, user data export, archive uploads and email sending

services:
  fittrackee-db:
    container_name: fittrackee-db
    # Always backup the database before FitTrackee upgrade when the new version
    # includes database migrations.
    #
    # Please refer to the PostgreSQL and PostGIS documentation before upgrading
    # image version.
    # Warning: Starting with version 18, PGDATA has changed, see:
    # https://hub.docker.com/_/postgres#pgdata
    #
    # Warning: there is no official image for PostGIS on ARM platforms yet, see:
    # https://github.com/postgis/docker-postgis/issues/216
    # The workaround is to build PostGIS image locally.
    image: postgis/postgis:18-3.6-alpine
    env_file:
      - .env
    volumes:
      - ${HOST_DATABASE_DIR:-./data/db}:/var/lib/postgresql
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "pg_isready -U $${POSTGRES_USER} -d $${POSTGRES_DB}"]
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 15s
      retries: 3
    networks:
      - internal_network
    restart: unless-stopped

  fittrackee:
    container_name: fittrackee
    env_file:
      - .env
# Image from Docker Hub
    image: fittrackee/fittrackee:v1.3.4
# Uncomment following line to build image instead of using pre-built image
#    build: .
    volumes:
      - ${HOST_UPLOAD_DIR:-./data/uploads}:/usr/src/app/uploads
      - ${HOST_STATICMAP_CACHE_DIR:-./data/staticmap_cache}:/usr/src/app/.staticmap_cache
# Comment the following line when logging to stdout
      - ${HOST_LOG_DIR:-./data/logs}:/usr/src/app/logs
    post_start:
# Remove '/usr/src/app/logs' directory when logging to stdout
      - command: chown -R fittrackee:fittrackee /usr/src/app/uploads /usr/src/app/.staticmap_cache /usr/src/app/logs
        user: root
    ports:
      - "${HOST_APP_PORT:-5000}:5000"
    command: 'sh docker-entrypoint.sh'
    depends_on:
      fittrackee-db:
        condition: service_healthy
# Uncomment the following lines for API rate limit, user data export, archive uploads and email sending
#      fittrackee-redis:
#        condition: service_healthy
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "wget --spider http://127.0.0.1:5000/api/check-db || exit 1"]
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 15s
      retries: 3
    networks:
      - external_network
      - internal_network
    restart: unless-stopped

repo: https://github.com/SamR1/FitTrackee

  image: fittrackee/fittrackee:v1.3.4
  port: 5000

quirks:
  - "POSTGIS IS MANDATORY, AND A PLAIN MANAGED POSTGRES WILL NOT DO. Pass db_extensions ['postgis'] to deploy_compose. Migration 59 adds a geoalchemy2 Geometry column and a geospatial GiST index, and FitTrackee NEVER runs CREATE EXTENSION itself. The entrypoint runs 'ftcli db upgrade || exit 1' before gunicorn, so without the extension the container exits 1 and crash-loops."
  - "DATABASE_URL IS THE VARIABLE THAT SELECTS THE REAL DATABASE. Upstream's compose ships its own postgis container (service fittrackee-db) whose data goes to a bind mount inside the project directory, which is what a source re-upload replaces and what dies with the VM. DELETE the fittrackee-db service, its depends_on entry and its volume. redu emits DATABASE_URL=postgresql://... so it can be passed straight through. deploy_compose only APPENDS to the project .env and never edits your compose, so put DATABASE_URL in the service's environment: block; an environment: entry beats env_file."
  - "PROVE THE DATABASE WIRING AFTER BOOT, BOTH HALVES. Positive: the sqlalchemy one-liner printing database name, inet_server_addr() and user count; the address must be the private IP of the managed database VM. Negative: 'docker ps | grep -c fittrackee-db' must be 0 AND 'docker ps | grep -c fittrackee' must be at least 1."
  - "NOBODY BECOMES ADMINISTRATOR BY SIGNING UP. YOU CREATE THE OWNER AT DEPLOY TIME WITH THE CLI. POST /api/auth/register creates an account with the default 'user' role and is_active False. With EMAIL_URL empty no confirmation email is sent, so an anonymous signup produces an account that CANNOT log in. Run 'docker exec fittrackee ftcli users create <username> --email <email> --role owner' after the container is healthy, and CONFIRM THE EMAIL WITH THE USER FIRST."
  - "THE REGISTRATION SETTING HAS A FIRST-USER CARVE-OUT AND IT IS NOT AN ENV VAR. max_users on the app_config row; is_registration_enabled is (max_users == 0 OR nb_users < max_users), default 0 meaning unlimited. Setting max_users to 1 with zero users still leaves registration OPEN. THE ONLY THING THAT CLOSES THE FIRST SLOT IS FILLING IT: create the owner with ftcli first, THEN PATCH /api/config with max_users."
  - "TEST THE BEHAVIOUR, NOT THE FLAG. GET /api/config reports is_registration_enabled, a derived value. The check that means something is a real anonymous POST /api/auth/register, which must answer 403."
  - "SET APP_SECRET_KEY EXPLICITLY AND REUSE THE SAME VALUE ON EVERY REDEPLOY. It is the JWT signing key; change it and everyone is logged out and outstanding reset links die."

Add a busybox:1.37 init service running 'chown -R 1000:1000' over both volumes with the app depending on it via service_completed_successfully. Set GUNICORN_LOG=- and leave APP_LOG unset so no logs volume is needed."

  - "THE REGISTRATION SETTING HAS A FIRST-USER CARVE-OUT AND IT IS NOT AN ENV VAR. max_users on the app_config row; is_registration_enabled is (max_users == 0 OR nb_users < max_users), default 0 meaning unlimited.
